_m4_consent_registry.public_signals: [dogTagId, purpose, relayer, nullifier, R, recordType, deadline] - NO subject, NO keyHash. Order is frozen with the M3 VK (circuits/README.consent.md).
_m4_consent_registry._selector_collision_WARNING: recordVerificationZK(uint256[2],uint256[2][2],uint256[2],uint256[7]) = 0xdd080593, which is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the RETIRED Level-A 4-arg selector (see _verification_registry_redeploy) - same ABI shape, COMPLETELY different pub semantics (Level-A pub[3]=subject/pub[4]=nullifier/pub[6]=R vs Level-B pub[3]=nullifier/pub[4]=R/pub[6]=deadline). A stale pre-PR#7 client aimed at this registry would DISPATCH rather than bounce, but fails closed twice (R!=profileRoot, then a Level-A proof cannot verify against the consent VK). Conversely a Level-B client aimed at the LIVE Level-A registry 0x4E2f0996 (which only dispatches the 6-arg 0x423a45b6) gets the bare `execution reverted, data: 0x` - the exact confusing symptom from data/dogtag-zkfail-z9. Check the ADDRESS first when debugging either.

m5_requirements.profileRoot: M5 MUST set profileRoot(dogTagId) = R, the per-tag Merkle root of the M1-engine tree (3 reserved owner leaves + attribute leaves). The SBT already stores profileRoot as bytes32 - NO SBT change is needed for M4. The registry asserts R == profileRoot(dogTagId); this is the ONLY place dogTagId <-> R is bound (the circuit deliberately does not).
m5_requirements.issue_the_root: M5 MUST ALSO issue(R) the per-tag root into a DogTagIssuer clone, not only setProfileRoot. The registry keeps the Level-A revocation path (resolve rootIssuer[R] -> clone, require isValid(R)), so a root that is only set as profileRoot and never issued reverts 'unknown root' on EVERY verify. This preserves revocation under Level-B: revoke(R) stops the tag verifying.
m5_requirements.custodial_mint: D1: mint to a neutral custodian, never the owner. The registry reads profileRoot for the binding and ownerOf for token EXISTENCE only (value DISCARDED, never compared), so a custodial ownerOf is correct and inert - ConsentRegistry.t.sol proves verification passes with ownerOf == custodian. The ownerOf call is NOT an owner-identity check: it exists because DogTagSBT.burn (GDPR-erasure) does not clear profileRoot[id], so R == profileRoot still passes for an erased tag, and OZ ownerOf (_requireOwned) reverting on a burned token is what fails erasure closed - see test_burned_tag_cannot_verify.
m5_requirements.profileRoot_is_mutable_KNOWN_GAP: OPEN SPEC QUESTION, KNOWN + ACCEPTED while Level-B is not live; M5 MUST resolve it. R == profileRoot(dogTagId) is the SOLE tag<->owner binding, and DogTagSBT.setProfileRoot is MUTABLE post-issuance by issuerOf[id] or ANY AUTHORITY_ROLE holder. With no ownerOf identity gate, a compromised issuer/authority can build a tree whose three reserved owner leaves it controls, issue(R2) it via its own whitelisted clone, setProfileRoot(victimTag, R2), and record a Verified for a victim tag - a forgery Level-A prevented by requiring BOTH ownerOf == subject AND keyOf(subject) == keyHash, both owner-controlled. M5 must resolve it (e.g. append-only/immutable profileRoot post-issuance, or a status == Active gate). Deliberately NOT fixed in M4: the SBT hardening belongs with the M5 issuance rework, and no consumer points at this registry until M7.

m7_cutover._note: Repoint these at 0x53F988Ae0124b96069d90CBC78E6245FeB01E125 ONLY when the apps prove against the M3 consent VK and Level-B custodial tags exist (M5). Repointing earlier breaks the live flow: today's clients send Level-A proofs. This is the same consumer list the 4-arg redeploy walked (see RedeployVerificationRegistry.s.sol).

NOTE (M8): the owner-blind Verified has a DIFFERENT topic0 than the Level-A one - stacks/indexer/api/src/chain.rs decodes by Verified::SIGNATURE_HASH and will silently skip Level-B events until M8 teaches it the new shape (dogTagId, relayer, purpose, nullifier, deadline, ts).
m7_cutover.backend_zk_path: stacks/vet/api/src/chain.rs (the recordVerificationZK sol! ABI is the 6-arg Level-A shape and must become 4-arg) + src/verify.rs. The ECDSA recordVerification path has NO Level-B equivalent (see _levelb_ecdsa_path).
m7_cutover.docs_normative_levelA_semantics: These carry the NORMATIVE Level-A verify semantics (the subject-bearing Verified event, the keyOf/ownerOf==subject checks, the pub=[dogTagId,purpose,relayer,subject,nullifier,keyHash,R] vector, the ECDSA path) and go STALE the moment Level-B is the live path - they are deliberately untouched by M4 (Level-A is still live and they describe it accurately), but M7 MUST revise them, not just swap addresses: docs/architecture.md (§4.1 contract set + §4.7 VerificationRegistry normative body), docs/implementation.md (§2.6 'Three new contracts' + the §11.8 normative bodies), docs/ROLE_APPS.md (the contract list + the verifier-role descriptions).
m7_cutover.docs_dpia: docs/DPIA.md is a self-declared LIVING document that 'MUST be refreshed whenever the on-chain data model, the verification subsystem, or the erasure flow change'. Level-B changes all three: the Verified linkage row (line ~36) is scored on `subject`+dogTagId+relayer and its mitigation is 'fresh per-pet subject' - under Level-B there IS no subject, so the row must be RE-SCORED, not just edited. The re-scoring itself needs a data-protection judgement (DPO/captain) and is deliberately NOT done while Level-B is not live - crediting the live system with a privacy improvement it does not yet have is the dangerous direction to be wrong in for a regulatory artifact. M4 instead added docs/DPIA.md section 2.1, a FORWARD-LOOKING note recording the refresh as QUEUED and naming the three rows that must be re-scored (verification-event linkage, wallet<->SBT link, and the erasure-flow burn mitigation); every current Level-A risk row/rating/mitigation is untouched and still accurate. M7 MUST perform the actual re-scoring, and GDPR Art. 35 wants it done BEFORE processing starts, i.e. before the cutover - not after.

_m4_consent_registry._levelb_ecdsa_path: There is deliberately NO ECDSA recordVerification on this registry. That path asserts ownerOf(dogTagId) == subject, which under D1 (custodial mint) resolves to the custodian and can never match a real owner - it is structurally dead under Level-B, and its subject-revealing Verified event would undo the circuit's purpose. Legacy ECDSA verification keeps working, unchanged, on the Level-A registry 0x4E2f0996 for as long as Level-A tags exist. If Level-B ever needs a non-ZK fallback that is a NEW spec decision (the owner has no on-chain identity to sign as), not a port of the Level-A path.
_m4_consent_registry._supersedes_stale_deploy: This address REPLACES the first M4 deploy 0x57A2998... (kept above as VerificationRegistryConsent_preErasureGate_legacy, block 194489, runtime 6179 bytes). That instance was deployed BEFORE the review-round hardening that added the ownerOf token-existence gate, so its bytecode LACKS the erasure gate: a GDPR-burned tag would still verify there. It was never live and no consumer ever pointed at it. This redeploy (runtime 6317 bytes) carries the gate and is byte-identical to the committed source, so the recorded address and the shipped code agree - which is the point: a canonical address whose bytecode differs from source is the same landmine class as data/dogtag-zkfail-z9. Do NOT use 0x57A2998.
